lexicon.name: DanaOS
lexicon.description: DanaOS is an industrial operating substrate for bounded agent execution: it preserves operational objects and evidence, routes governed missions through reusable execution graphs, and exposes operator-facing tools for authoring, inspection, and retrieval. This first model covers the active monorepo source rooted at the DanaOS checkout; archived prior art and proposed surfaces are named only where they affect an active boundary.

context.name: Operational Substrate
context.description: Persists industrial ontology, evidence, procedures, tasks, missions, loop records, and audit information, and serves bounded query and service surfaces to runtimes and agents.
context.annotation: The Rust ODB core is the durable implementation boundary. The repository documentation describes broader future contents, while the executable objects and APIs establish the current task, mission, loop, graph, vector, and audit surfaces.
context.code-link: Defines the persisted ontology, observation, procedure, task, mission, artifact, loop, and governance record shapes.
Exposes service routes for loop records, checkpoints, heartbeats, and audit operations.

concept.name: Durable Operational Object
concept.description: An identified object that carries operational meaning across requests, such as an ontology entity, observation, procedure, policy, mission, artifact, or task.
concept.annotation: The object family is broader than a conventional row: its variants preserve evidence, provenance, governance state, or executable context that later agent work can consume.
concept.code-link: Rust records in this file represent durable domain entities, observations, procedures, policies, missions, artifacts, and provenance blocks.

concept.name: Mission Task Record
concept.description: The durable operational record of a bounded mission or task, including its steps, runtime state, outcomes, and references to artifacts and evidence.
concept.annotation: Task runtime fields and STAR stage records are bounded by explicit service limits; terminal and stale states are exposed through the loop and task APIs.
concept.code-link: Defines the durable task and mission identities and their operational fields.
Applies bounded runtime-state storage for task steps, outcomes, and STAR stage records.

concept.name: Operational Query
concept.description: A structured request for durable, graph, vector, time-series, or industrial DQL information used to retrieve context for diagnosis and bounded execution.
concept.annotation: Query surfaces are separate from the agents that interpret their results; retrieval can be exact, indexed, graph-based, or industrial-function backed.
concept.code-link: Defines storage filtering inputs for querying persisted records.
Defines graph query input at the service boundary.
Registers industrial DQL functions used by the query executor.

concept.name: Access Authority
concept.description: The principal, role, scope, and policy context under which a caller may read, invoke, or mutate a substrate capability.
concept.annotation: The service derives authorization context and rejects unauthorized or forbidden requests at the service boundary; agent authority bands separately constrain leaf execution.
concept.code-link: Carries the request principal and authorization context and defines the service role vocabulary used in authorization decisions.

concept.name: ODB Client Contract
concept.description: The client-side HTTP contract through which runtimes and front doors read canonical mission definitions, retrieve context, and persist or resume operational records.
concept.annotation: Clients adapt their caller needs to ODB service routes; they do not own the durable record model or silently replace the substrate with local state.
concept.code-link: Reads and writes mission, task, artifact, and resume state for the agent runtime.
Provides the CLI's ODB request adapter.

context.name: Governed Agent Runtime
context.description: Accepts an external mission, resolves its governed control surface and workflow binding, then dispatches a bounded STAR leaf or a resolved workflow and returns one traced outcome.
context.annotation: External requests enter through the gateway; the bare leaf escape hatch is explicitly reserved for unit and gym tests and is not wired to user-facing commands.
context.code-link: Single external invocation boundary that binds, dispatches, traces, and returns the governed result.
Post-gate STAR leaf runner with authority bands, routing, tools, and optional memory.

concept.name: Mission Binding
concept.description: The decision that maps mission text and caller context to an admitted agent, mission class, workflow or leaf target, authority bands, and post-bind action.
concept.annotation: Binding can curate a pin, defer with evidence, or refuse. A live bound mission is admitted only for the runtime's accepted decision forms and carries the resolved target metadata into dispatch.
concept.code-link: Carries the binding decision, target, and routing metadata.
Maps classified intent and extracted slots to a workflow binding.
Routes mission text through the binding decision path and post-bind policy.

concept.name: STAR Leaf
concept.description: A bounded See, Think, Act, Reflect execution unit that consumes an authority envelope and context packet, may use allowlisted tools, and emits an outcome with evidence and trace fields.
concept.annotation: Tool and token budgets come from the authority envelope; memory recall can block or force recomputation, and the runner records phase and outcome information.
concept.code-link: Executes the STAR phases and produces the normalized leaf outcome.
Normalizes post-gate leaf execution into an outcome and channel-facing payload.

concept.name: Agent Workflow
concept.description: A resolved graph of agent nodes and edges that performs a multi-step mission after binding, with graph steps, recommendations, answer, and durable artifact references in its result.
concept.annotation: Workflow definitions can be read from an ODB-canonical deployment or from disk as an authoring fallback; the resolved graph remains the runtime's executable shape.
concept.code-link: Resolves the workflow graph and its nodes for an agent invocation.
Captures workflow steps, bind result, answer, recommendations, trace, and ODB artifact id.
Binds, dispatches, executes, and returns the workflow result.

concept.name: Control Surface
concept.description: The resolved authority and policy configuration that determines which execution layers, tools, pins, and authority bands a mission may use.
concept.annotation: Production control surfaces validate pin maps and authority before the gateway dispatches; the leaf receives authority from the caller rather than hardcoding it.
concept.code-link: Represents resolved control-surface state and its trace fields.
Resolves control-surface configuration used by the gateway.

concept.name: Advisory Outcome
concept.description: A governed answer, recommendation, refusal, decline, or blocked result returned to a caller after the runtime applies its authority and safety boundaries.
concept.annotation: Current DanaOS agent posture is advisory: the gateway returns recommendations or a governed refusal/decline and does not execute a refused mission. External actuation remains behind separate ODB policy guards.
concept.code-link: Carries decision, execution flag, status, answer, recommendations, and trace for one governed invocation.
Constructs a refusal result without execution.
Implements fail-closed policy guards for actuation-class proxy requests.

context.name: Loop Orchestration
context.description: Runs a configured goal through a bounded plan graph, alternating planning, action, observation, evaluation, compression, completion, and fail-safe or human-interrupt routes.
context.annotation: The loop can drive ZCode or an agent runner. It owns iteration state and convergence decisions while delegating leaf execution to the selected runner.
context.code-link: Builds the plan graph and its conditional routes.
Runs the compiled loop against a plan definition and target repository.

concept.name: Loop Definition
concept.description: The validated plan describing the goal, action target, phase bounds, evaluation regime, and optional agent or ZCode execution settings.
concept.annotation: The definition is authored as plan configuration and is consumed by graph construction; the wizard supplies an interactive creation path but does not itself execute the loop.
concept.code-link: Interactive creation path for loop definitions.
Consumes the validated definition to choose the runner and graph routes.

concept.name: Loop State
concept.description: The evolving state of one loop run: iteration, pending prompt or mission, runner result, observation, evaluation, context budget, status, and human-interrupt information.
concept.annotation: Bounds are checked before planning and evaluation routes distinguish done, failed, interrupted, bounds-exceeded, compression, and next-iteration outcomes.
concept.code-link: Defines the state fields shared by plan, act, observe, eval, and routing nodes.
Chooses continuation, compression, completion, interruption, or fail-safe based on evaluation and bounds.

concept.name: Loop Record
concept.description: The durable registry identity and status projection for a loop, used to report liveness, stale runs, terminal records, and program progression across process boundaries.
concept.code-link: Defines the loop registry record projected to ODB.
Advances program phases using loop records and their terminal state.

concept.name: Loop Bounds And Verdict
concept.description: The explicit limit and evaluation result that determines whether a loop may continue, compress context, complete, interrupt for a human, or enter a fail-safe state.
concept.annotation: Maximum iterations, wall-clock or cost limits, and evaluation outcomes are checked in the graph; an exceeded bound becomes a terminal bounded outcome.
concept.code-link: Contains loop-specific bounds checks and exceeded-reason calculation.
Applies bounds before a cycle enters planning.

context.name: Execution Kernel
context.description: Provides generic LangGraph-backed graph compilation, invocation, tracing, resumption, bounds, and leaf-executor contracts shared by the agent and loop consumers.
context.annotation: The kernel supplies graph mechanics and normalized leaf contracts; consumer packages supply their state schemas, node wiring, domain outcomes, and leaf implementations.
context.code-link: Shared compile, invoke, trace, describe, and resume wrapper.
Defines the consumer-independent leaf executor seam.

concept.name: Graph Engine
concept.description: The mechanics service that compiles consumer-supplied nodes and edges and invokes or resumes the resulting graph with a recursion limit and optional checkpointer.
concept.code-link: Implements the shared graph lifecycle and trace-bearing invocation.

concept.name: Leaf Outcome
concept.description: The normalized result exchanged between an outer plan graph and a bounded leaf, carrying status, evidence, cost, trace reference, and summary.
concept.code-link: Defines the common outcome shape used by loop and agent leaves.

context.name: Memory And Capability Libraries
context.description: Supplies reusable cross-cutting capabilities for memory retrieval and content, authentication and principals, external resolver contracts, and structural vocabulary loading.
context.annotation: These libraries are imported by runtime and product surfaces and do not themselves define a process boundary; their contracts keep callers from duplicating storage, identity, or provider policy.
context.code-link: Implements hybrid lexical and vector retrieval over memory evidence.
Implements OAuth token acquisition and refresh for runtime and operator flows.

concept.name: Memory Evidence
concept.description: Retrievable or resolvable content with an identity, provenance, validity, and optional write-back policy that can inform a later agent turn.
concept.annotation: Hybrid retrieval filters invalid results and content stores resolve or atomically write content; the STAR runner decides whether recalled evidence is accepted or recomputed.
concept.code-link: Combines lexical and vector evidence into recall results.
Resolves and atomically writes content across configured storage tiers.

concept.name: Principal And Token
concept.description: The authenticated caller identity and bearer credential used to authorize runtime, operator, and on-behalf-of requests.
concept.annotation: Token claims are decoded for client-side principal extraction, while resource services are responsible for signature validation; cached tokens refresh before expiry.
concept.code-link: Acquires and refreshes client-credential, exchange, authorization-code, and device-code tokens.
Represents the persisted principal extracted from claims.

concept.name: Resolver Contract
concept.description: A fetch-only contract for resolving one class of external facts into a result with provider identity, provenance URI, TTL, and write-back fields.
concept.annotation: Resolvers do not perform cache lookup, authorization, or substrate mutation; those responsibilities stay with the registry, policy layer, or caller.
concept.code-link: Defines the provider-facing fetch-only resolver protocol.
Defines the resolved fact and provenance/write-back shape.
Registers resolvers and dispatches requests by supported prefix.

concept.name: Structural Pack Contract
concept.description: A domain-blind declarative vocabulary of kinds, relations, and containment that maps vertical terms to the core Place, Asset, and Signal spine.
concept.annotation: Pack loading fails closed on unknown keys, duplicate kinds, invalid core supertypes, and dangling relation or containment endpoints.
concept.code-link: Represents a validated structural vocabulary pack.
Validates and rejects malformed pack documents as a whole.

context.name: World Models And Operational Packs
context.description: Provides mechanistic simulators and learned model families that act as WorldModel backends, together with domain-specific operational packs and replay/evaluation artifacts.
context.annotation: The model-family tree contains active simulator and Kairos learned-family implementations. Their role is to supply world-state or predictive capability to runtime consumers; this first model does not treat individual experiments as separate domain concepts.
context.code-link: Defines the package boundary and model-family ownership guidance for active model sources.

concept.name: World Model
concept.description: A model-family backend that represents, simulates, predicts, or evaluates a domain world for an agent or loop.
concept.annotation: The repository contains both mechanistic simulator manifests and learned time-series models; they share a consumer role without sharing one implementation class.
concept.code-link: Mechanistic building simulator evaluation path.
Learned time-series model family used by Kairos experiments.

concept.name: Operational Pack
concept.description: A domain-specific bundle of vocabulary, rules, procedures, or fixtures that makes a runtime useful in an industrial vertical.
concept.annotation: Operational packs under model families are distinct from the proposed domain-blind structural packs in the capability library; the two surfaces have different ownership and contracts.
concept.code-link: Declares an executable simulator package and its domain configuration.
Scores the domain-specific simulator outcome.

context.name: Governance And Data Agents
context.description: Provides peer agents that govern ontology and adaptation decisions, retrieve data with provenance, and coach humans through agent or loop authoring.
context.annotation: The ontologist is a separate peer governance package over ODB; the Librarian returns data and provenance and carries an NG5 boundary against diagnosis; Dana is an authoring coach with policy-aware tools.
context.code-link: Executes the implemented promote review path and writes a review artifact through ODB contracts.

concept.name: Ontology Review
concept.description: A governed review of a candidate ontology, catalog, adaptation, or memory artifact that may produce a promotion decision and durable review evidence.
concept.annotation: The implemented promote path reads a candidate, runs binding checks, and writes an artifact only when the review passes; defer and rollback are accepted contract values but are not implemented in this path.
concept.code-link: Carries review pass/failure and phase result information.
Applies adaptation candidate review checks before promotion.

concept.name: Librarian Answer
concept.description: A data-only response assembled from allowlisted ODB and external sources, with source provenance and status suitable for a caller to interpret.
concept.annotation: The Librarian envelope validators reject task or diagnosis claims in source and skill fields; its purpose is retrieval and provenance, not diagnosis.
concept.code-link: Defines the constrained answer envelope and NG5 validation.
Fuses source outcomes into a provenance-bearing result.
Builds the retrieval agent's tool-enabled execution.

concept.name: Authoring Coach
concept.description: Dana's guided authoring surface for discovering capabilities, validating loop definitions, writing loop artifacts, and promoting agent or pack work under policy.
concept.annotation: Wizard tools validate target paths and loop definitions and refuse unsafe or malformed writes; the coach is an authoring surface, not the loop executor.
concept.code-link: Implements the wizard's guarded tool surface, validation, and authoring writes.
Represents the wizard's structured result.

concept.name: Runtime Ontology Adapter
concept.description: A public adapter that loads visible ODB skills and packages draft-only ontology review evidence for Console and Enterprise consumers.
concept.annotation: This adapter is separate from the canonical ontologist governance agent. The distinction prevents a draft review integration from being mistaken for the authoritative governance process.
concept.code-link: Loads visibility-filtered skills from ODB for the runtime adapter.
Defines the evidence manifest passed through the adapter boundary.

context.name: External Data Adapters
context.description: Implements provider-specific resolver leaves that fetch external facts through declared prefixes while leaving caching, authorization, and substrate mutation to their callers.
context.annotation: The resolver contract assigns providers a fetch-only responsibility; provider packages live under dana-adapters and are consumed through the resolver registry or Librarian broker.
context.code-link: Defines the adapter tier and its provider boundary.

concept.name: Resolver Adapter
concept.description: A provider implementation of the resolver contract for one or more external data prefixes.
concept.code-link: Provider resolver implementations for Honeywell external data.
Bridges Librarian requests to ODB-brokered resolver instances.

context.name: Front Doors And Product Surfaces
context.description: Exposes DanaOS capabilities through the unified CLI, interactive Console, and end-user product surfaces, including agent invocation, ODB inspection, loop control, authentication, authoring, and ontology review.
context.annotation: Front doors coordinate existing runtime contracts and persist their own session or activity projections where needed; they do not replace the ODB or agent gateway.
context.code-link: Dispatches the unified dana command surface.
Creates the FastAPI Console application and mounts its routes and web shell.

concept.name: Dana CLI
concept.description: The unified command-line front door that dispatches agent, ODB, loop, memory, model, librarian, wizard, and governance operations.
concept.code-link: Builds and dispatches the CLI command tree.
Connects a loop-agent command to the agent gateway and loop runner.

concept.name: Dana Console
concept.description: An interactive debug and operator surface for invocations, traces, loop state, ODB exploration, graph authoring, and ontology review.
concept.code-link: Creates the Console server and mounts the product APIs.
Persists Console activities, invocations, chat sessions, and ontology review state.
Coordinates the review evidence completion and freeze operation at the Console boundary.

concept.name: Enterprise Workspace
concept.description: An end-user DanaOS application surface that hosts authenticated agent sessions, document-backed retrieval, and governed draft publication over the shared runtime and ODB contracts.
concept.annotation: This surface is a consumer of the substrate and runtime; its workspace and publish flows preserve product-level review and evidence rather than redefining agent execution.
concept.code-link: Coordinates authenticated enterprise sessions, draft inspection, evidence, and publishing steps.
Runs one enterprise conversation turn through the runtime boundary.

relationship.name: records governed execution in
relationship.description: The agent gateway binds and executes a mission, while the ODB mission and task records preserve runtime artifacts, outcomes, and trace references for later inspection or resume.
relationship.annotation: The gateway constructs a result with trace and artifact fields and uses the ODB mission client for canonical definitions and resume state; the record API is the durable counterpart.
relationship.code-link: Gateway path that resolves ODB-backed definitions and returns traced execution metadata.
Service routes that persist and query loop/task runtime records.

relationship.name: reads and persists through
relationship.description: The runtime uses the ODB client contract for canonical mission definitions, artifact references, and resume state while the ODB remains the owning durable substrate.
relationship.code-link: Constructs the ODB mission client when an ODB-backed invocation is configured.
Implements the runtime-facing ODB client.

relationship.name: selects a leaf for
relationship.description: A successful binding determines whether the gateway dispatches the post-gate STAR leaf or a workflow path, carrying authority and mission metadata into execution.
relationship.annotation: The gateway performs the bind first and only then dispatches; the leaf documents the one-way gateway to runner layering.
relationship.code-link: Dispatches the resolved bind to the selected execution path.
Receives the post-gate authority and mission inputs.

relationship.name: selects a workflow for
relationship.description: Workflow-axis bindings carry a pinned workflow identity and version into graph resolution and execution.
relationship.code-link: Consumes the bound mission and workflow key to execute a graph.

relationship.name: uses graph mechanics from
relationship.description: The agent workflow supplies domain graph wiring while the shared kernel supplies compilation, invocation, tracing, and resume mechanics.
relationship.annotation: The consumer owns graph resolution and state; the dependency direction keeps LangGraph mechanics in dana-exec.
relationship.code-link: Workflow execution imports and uses the shared graph engine seam.
Provides the mechanics used by consumers.

relationship.name: runs through
relationship.description: Loop orchestration supplies its own LoopState and node routes, then compiles and runs them through the shared GraphEngine contract.
relationship.code-link: Builds the loop graph using shared execution mechanics.

relationship.name: projects runtime state into
relationship.description: The in-process LoopState changes each iteration; the registry LoopRecord and ODB loop APIs preserve a cross-process status and heartbeat projection.
relationship.annotation: The exact serialization boundary varies by execution mode, so this model treats the record as a durable projection rather than claiming every state field is stored identically.
relationship.code-link: Defines the durable registry projection.
Defines the ODB-side durable loop record.

relationship.name: can delegate iterations to
relationship.description: When a plan targets an agent, its plan node builds a mission and its agent runner invokes the bounded agent runtime for the act step.
relationship.annotation: The CLI supplies the gateway as the injected agent invocation seam; loop code does not need to import the agent package directly.
relationship.code-link: Adapts agent invocation into the loop runner port.
Wires the CLI loop-agent path to `invoke_agent`.

relationship.name: emits
relationship.description: The STAR runner's native result is normalized into the shared leaf outcome vocabulary for outer graph routing and reporting.
relationship.code-link: Produces the bounded STAR result.
Defines the normalized outcome vocabulary.

relationship.name: returns a governed
relationship.description: The bind decision and post-bind execution determine whether a caller receives an answer or recommendation, a refusal, a decline, or a blocked result.
relationship.code-link: Returns the governed decision and outcome envelope to external callers.

relationship.name: informs
relationship.description: The leaf can resolve keyed memory through the ODB-backed memory port, verify recalled evidence, recompute when required, and write back an episodic rationale.
relationship.annotation: Memory participation is conditional on the configured ODB path and the runner's decision protocol; unavailable or invalid memory can produce a blocked or recompute outcome.
relationship.code-link: Builds the ODB-backed memory port for a leaf mission.
Completes the memory decision path and folds its result into the STAR outcome.

relationship.name: supplies retrieval for
relationship.description: Memory retrieval and content resolution use ODB-backed lexical, vector, and content surfaces to recover evidence for a later turn.
relationship.code-link: Combines retrieval sources into memory evidence.

relationship.name: supplies world context to
relationship.description: Model-family implementations and simulator fixtures can provide domain world state, predictions, or evaluation inputs to agent workflows and their bounded missions.
relationship.annotation: The common consumer contract is documented at the package boundary; individual model families expose different APIs, so this first model leaves the exact injection path qualified.
relationship.code-link: Documents model families as WorldModel backends consumed by runtime packages.

relationship.name: defines domain vocabulary for
relationship.description: Operational packs and simulator manifests describe the domain entities, signals, scenarios, and scoring terms that a world model represents or evaluates.
relationship.code-link: Binds a simulator implementation to its domain configuration.

relationship.name: dispatches requests to
relationship.description: The registry selects a provider adapter by supported prefix and returns its resolver result without taking ownership of provider policy or substrate mutation.
relationship.code-link: Dispatches a resolver request to the matching registered provider.
Implements a brokered resolver bridge used by the Librarian.

relationship.name: contributes sourced facts to
relationship.description: Provider resolver results become source entries in the Librarian's data-only answer, retaining provider identity and provenance for the caller.
relationship.code-link: Projects resolver outcomes into source records.

relationship.name: supplies data to
relationship.description: The Librarian uses an ODB tool port to search documents, read documents, query the ontology graph, and read Layer-A skills before constructing its sourced answer.
relationship.code-link: Implements the Librarian's ODB-backed search, document, graph, and skill reads.

relationship.name: reviews and promotes
relationship.description: The peer ontologist reviews candidate runtime artifacts and catalog or adaptation changes, promoting only candidates that pass the binding checks supported by the current implementation.
relationship.annotation: A failed promote review writes no artifact. The governance agent is a separate peer package over ODB rather than an internal ODB control plane.
relationship.code-link: Runs the review and promotion boundary.
Persists the successful review artifact through ODB.

relationship.name: persists review evidence as
relationship.description: A successful governance review becomes a durable ODB review artifact so later runtime and operator surfaces can inspect the decision and its evidence.
relationship.code-link: Writes a passed review artifact to ODB.

relationship.name: guides authoring of
relationship.description: The wizard guides users through loop creation and validates loop definitions before guarded tool writes create or update loop artifacts.
relationship.code-link: Validates the loop definition before an authoring write.
Writes a validated loop artifact under the wizard's path guards.

relationship.name: supplies draft review evidence to
relationship.description: The runtime adapter packages visible skills and ontology evidence for the Console's draft-only review and freeze flow.
relationship.annotation: This is an adapter integration, while authoritative promotion remains the ontologist's governance responsibility.
relationship.code-link: Consumes runtime review evidence at the Console boundary.

relationship.name: invokes through
relationship.description: The CLI's ask, run, workflow, librarian, and loop-agent commands dispatch into the governed runtime and its binding boundary.
relationship.code-link: CLI command that reaches the ask/runtime path.
CLI loop-agent command wiring to governed agent invocation.

relationship.name: inspects and projects
relationship.description: The Console reads invocation and ODB-backed run state, persists a local activity/session projection, and exposes traces, loop state, and review operations for operators.
relationship.code-link: Persists local invocation, session, activity, and review projections.
Registers invocation artifacts for Console inspection.

relationship.name: authorizes requests from
relationship.description: CLI and runtime clients acquire tokens and derive principals to access ODB and governed operations under the configured authority.
relationship.code-link: Constructs the token acquirer for the CLI login flow.
Resolves the runtime principal used by callers.

relationship.name: authorizes
relationship.description: The enterprise workspace derives a principal and bearer token for authenticated sessions and governed document or runtime operations.
relationship.code-link: Applies enterprise-side authorization decisions for a principal and resource action.
Connects enterprise calls to the canonical IAM boundary.

relationship.name: constrains
relationship.description: Authenticated principal and service authorization establish the outer request authority, while mission binding resolves the narrower execution policy and authority bands.
relationship.annotation: The service and agent layers implement distinct enforcement points; this relationship describes their cooperation without collapsing service authorization into agent binding.
relationship.code-link: Resolves execution authority for a bound mission.
Enforces service-side request authority.
